newsitem.title: UK: Dlr steady in Europe but down from ealier levels.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady in Europe but down from ealier levels.

text.p: The dollar steadied in a quiet afternoon Europe, down from earlier highs against the mark and yen following a set of benign inflation and industrial output data from the U.S.
After rising briefly following the U.S. May consumer price figures, the dollar slipped back slightly amid the shrinking prospect of a near-term hike in U.S. interest rates.

"There was nothing too impressive in the CPI data, it really just confirms the U.S. is still in a low-inflation scenario, putting the argument for a U.S. rate hike any time soon on to the backburner," said a dealer at a Japanese bank.
U.S. May headline CPI data rose 0.1 percent against a 0.2 percent rise expected while core figure, ex food and energy, was up 0.2 percent as expected.
May industrial output was up 0.4 percent versus 0.2 forecast and capacity utilisation at 83.7 percent was a shade above expectations.
The dollar against the mark was trading at 1.7334/44, down from earlier levels above 1.7370 but above late Monday's level in Europe of 1.7295/05 marks.
Dollar/yen was also off session highs, trading at 113.38/48 after testing 113.79 earlier but little changed late Monday.

Dealers said afternoon trade was quiet and likely to remain so until the release of Japanese May trade balance data at 2350 GMT. The figures are expected to show a widening trade surplus with the U.S., a situation likely to be reinforced when the U.S. releases its trade data Thursday.
The focus on these numbers is more acute as they come just before this weekend's G7 summit in Denver, Colorado.

So far, markets have been relatively calm this week ahead of the trade data and the G7 and dealers said much of expected fall-out of any U.S.-Japan trade tension has largely been priced in to the market.

"I think the market is putting too much store into what comes out of the trade figures and the G7," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. "G7 will toe the line of previous meetings and the trade numbers will show the market what it already knows."

Although trade nerves and waning higher U.S. rate speculation has capped dollar progress, dollar/mark was still seen supported by optimism over progress towards a timely start of Europe's monetary union.
The EMU optimism kept the mark soft on its European crosses, which earlier tested a four-month low against the lira.
The Swiss franc was easier against the dollar and the mark, pressured earlier by the continued injection of liquidity into Swiss money markets by the Swiss National Bank.
Dollar/Swiss franc stood at 1.4462/72, down from an earlier high of 1.4515 but up from 1.4397/02 late Monday.
Sterling was stronger against the mark, mainly on the mark's weakness in Europe, and revisited the 57-month highs seen on Monday and Friday last week.
Sterling/mark was trading at 2.8407/12 in late trade from 2.8295/05 late Monday. Cable was at $1.6380/90 from $1.6349/54.
